newsitem.title: USA: China must fix farm issues to join WTO--Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: China must fix farm issues to join WTO--Barshefsky.

text.p: The United States will block Chinese accession to the World Trade Organization unless it resolves U.S. complaints over barriers to agricultural trade, U.S. Trade Representative nominee Charlene Barshefsky said Wednesday.

"Unless these agriculture issues are resolved, it doesn't much matter what else is in their accession package. WTO accession would be impossible to think of," Barshefsky said at her confirmation hearing before the Senate Finance Committee.
"We will be and have been very persistent on the agricultural issues. They are difficult issues," she added.

Barshefsky said China's bumper crop and the "spurious" use of sanitary and phytosanitary restrictions to block sales had created trade problems in wheat, citrus, meat, pork, poultry and a number of other commodities.
"China imposes rules that no other country imposes, not even Japan. And China has thus far refused in some sectors to take action," she said.
But she said China has agreed to alert the United States in advance to potential trade problems, to see if they can be resolved before they lead to bans.
